title: Dual-core chip multiprocessing with shared L2 cache
decision: Integrate two complete processor cores on a single die with a unified L2 cache shared between them
alternatives_or_rejected: A single larger out-of-order core targeting higher single-thread performance, or two cores each with private L2 caches
rationale: Commercial server workloads exhibit abundant thread-level parallelism; two cores deliver higher aggregate throughput than one wider core, and a shared L2 improves cache utilization while simplifying coherency between the cores
outcome: A dual-core chip delivering significantly higher throughput per socket on commercial benchmarks, with reduced off-chip coherency traffic compared to private-cache alternatives
weakest_point: The exact wording of the rationale; I am confident the dual-core/shared-L2 choice is central to the paper

title: On-chip L3 controller with off-chip L3 data arrays
decision: Place the L3 cache controller and tags on the processor die while locating the L3 data SRAMs on separate chips in the multi-chip module
alternatives_or_rejected: A fully on-die L3 (prohibitively large at the target capacity), or a fully off-chip L3 controller (higher latency and bandwidth constraints)
rationale: This hybrid approach saves processor die area for cores and L2 while allowing flexible L3 capacities; it also keeps L3 access latency lower than a purely off-chip solution
outcome: Scalable L3 configurations with lower access latency than prior off-chip-only designs, while preserving processor die area
weakest_point: Specific capacity numbers and exact latency claims may blend general product knowledge with the paper text
provenance_note: The architectural decision direction is from the paper; specific L3 capacity ranges may come from broader POWER4 product knowledge

title: Multi-banked shared L2 cache with crossbar interconnect
decision: Organize the shared L2 cache into multiple independent banks (slices) connected to the two cores via a crossbar rather than as a single monolithic array
alternatives_or_rejected: A single monolithic L2 bank that would serialize accesses from the two cores and limit bandwidth
rationale: Two aggressive out-of-order cores generate high concurrent demand for L2 bandwidth; a banked organization with a crossbar allows simultaneous independent accesses from both cores
outcome: Sufficient L2 bandwidth to feed both cores without serialization bottlenecks, supporting high throughput on memory-intensive commercial workloads
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly frames the banked/crossbar organization as a weighed decision with a monolithic L2 as the rejected alternative, or merely describes the chosen structure

title: Enterprise-class RAS with instruction retry and full ECC
decision: Implement full ECC on all caches and data paths, plus hardware instruction retry and other autonomous fault-recovery mechanisms
alternatives_or_rejected: Parity-only error detection without correction, or less extensive recovery that would require operating-system intervention on errors
rationale: POWER4 targets enterprise and mainframe-class reliability; transient soft errors must be detected, corrected, and recovered from silently without interrupting application execution
outcome: The ability to recover automatically from many transient hardware faults, achieving high system availability comparable to mainframe-class systems
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly contrasts ECC-plus-retry against parity-only as a rejected alternative, or simply describes the chosen RAS features

title: Aggressive out-of-order superscalar core architecture
decision: Implement a deeply pipelined, wide-issue out-of-order core with register renaming and speculative execution rather than a simpler in-order design
alternatives_or_rejected: A simpler in-order core, or a less aggressive out-of-order design with narrower issue and shallower speculation
rationale: High single-thread performance is still required to complement multi-core throughput; commercial workloads contain significant single-threaded components that benefit from aggressive instruction-level parallelism extraction
outcome: A high-IPC core capable of sustaining the deep pipeline and high frequency, delivering strong single-thread performance within the dual-core system
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly frames the core complexity as a weighed decision against simpler alternatives, or primarily describes the resulting microarchitecture
